newsitem.title: GERMANY: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST - JULY 4.
newsitem.headline: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST - JULY 4.

text.p: News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends

BERLIN - The Love Parade, a giant techno party expected to attract a million young people from around the world to Berlin on July 12, may be moved to other cities in future, its organisers say. This year's sponsors of the huge street party include Camel and German television and radio stations. (Reuter)

DUSSELDORF - Publishing company Madsack GmbH & Co of Hannover, the largest media company in the state of Lower Saxony, posts a drop in its advertising and publication-supplement business in 1997.(Handelsblatt)

FRANKFURT - The recent agreement between Deutsche Telekom, Kirch and Bertelsmann over the launch of digital television is criticised by the Association of Private Cable Network Providers (Anga). Anga questions Telekom's mandate to negotiate for private cable companies and apartment building owners which arrange cable service for their tenants. Telekom provides service to only about a third of the 16.7 million German households with a cable TV connection, Anga says. (Reuter)

COLOGNE - A majority of companies polled by a leading German insurance company say they are not prepared for the "Millennium bug" that threatens to bring the world's computers to a halt at the turn of the century. German reinsurer Cologne Re says 60 percent of the 124 companies polled say they have not yet fully analysed their computer systems, while 31 percent say they have done nothing at all. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Shares in German television channel Pro Sieben AG, due to be floated on the stock market on Monday, are likely to be more than 10 times over-subscribed, a spokesman for the company says. (Reuter)
MUNICH - Siemens AG says it has agreed on forming an alliance with a "leading global manufacturer of data communications products and solutions" but declines to name its partner.(Reuter)

BONN - Germany's new telecommunications regulatory chief, appointed this week by Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet, says his main focus will be to ensure a fair playing field for newcomers to the market. Klaus-Dieter Scheuerle, the director of the Post and Telecommunications Ministry's regulatory department, takes up his new job on January 1, 1998, when telecoms markets in Germany and most of Europe are opened to full competition. (Reuter)

BERLIN - The 500 largest German companies expanded sales in 1996, says newspaper Die Welt. Profits jumped 5.6 percent among the companies compared with 1995 to more than 3,475 billion marks, says Die Welt. Daimler-Benz AG remains the largest German company with sales of 106.3 billion marks and 290,000 employees.(Reuter)
